chunks: Al-Suli said: Al-Husayn ibn al-Jahm narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said:

Al-Ma'mun ascended the pulpit to inaugurate 'Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha (peace be upon him), and he said: O people! The allegiance of 'Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon them) has come to you. By Allah, had these names been recited over the deaf and the mute, they would be cured by Allah's permission.

key_terms.الصُّمِّ الْبُكْمِ: The deaf and the mute; mentioned as examples of those afflicted with incurable ailments who would be healed by the baraka of the Imams' names
key_terms.بيعة: Bay'a — the pledge of allegiance/inauguration; in this context, al-Ma'mun's formal proclamation of al-Ridha as heir apparent
key_terms.بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ: By Allah's permission — emphasizing that the healing comes from God, mediated through the blessed names

ai.seo_question: What did al-Ma'mun say about the names of Imam al-Ridha and his ancestors?
ai.summary: This narration recounts the historic moment in 201 AH when the Abbasid Caliph al-Ma'mun publicly proclaimed 'Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha (AS) as his successor and heir apparent. During the ceremony, al-Ma'mun declared the miraculous power inherent in the names of the Imams from the Prophetic household, stating that merely reciting their lineage would heal the deaf and the mute. The audience in Khurasan — the center of al-Ma'mun's power — witnessed this extraordinary claim, which reinforced Shia beliefs about the unique spiritual status of the Imams as a source of divine blessing and healing.
